chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah or Abu Ja'far (peace be upon them) said:
The prayer is not repeated due to blood that is not visible, except for the blood of menstruation, for its little or much in the garment, whether you see it or do not see it, is the same.

key_terms.قَلِيلَهُ وَ كَثِيرَهُ: Its little and much (small or large amount)

ai.seo_question: Does hidden blood invalidate prayer or require repetition according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the principle of *istishab al-salah* (presumption of validity) by exempting hidden impurities (*majhul al-dam*) from invalidating prayer, with menstrual blood as the sole exception due to its distinct jurisprudential status. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that minor, unseen blood does not break ritual purity, emphasizing the ease (*taysir*) in worship while maintaining strict standards for the primary impurity of menstruation.
